props.gloss_en: the mishnah does not list eating the Paschal lamb among the mitzvot that run until dawn -- so, per the mishnah, it is eaten only until midnight (the value the sugya supplies through R' Elazar ben Azarya)
the baraita: the evening Shema may be recited until dawn
the baraita: Hallel on Passover nights may be recited until dawn
the baraita: the Paschal lamb may be eaten until dawn
this [the mishnah] accords with R' Elazar ben Azarya
that [the baraita] accords with R' Akiva
R' Elazar ben Azarya: the Paschal lamb is eaten until midnight
R' Akiva: it was already said 'in haste' (Ex 12:11) -- the Paschal lamb is eaten until the hour of haste
(entertained) one might think the Paschal lamb is eaten by day, like other offerings
R' Akiva: 'on the night' teaches that it is eaten by night and not by day
'THAT night' comes to exclude another night: it is eaten on that night and not on another night
peace-offerings are eaten for two days and one night
(entertained) since the Pesach and peace-offerings are both of lesser sanctity, the Pesach would be eaten two nights in place of two days -- two nights and one day
R' Elazar ben Azarya derives 'not on another night' from 'you shall not leave any of it until morning' (Ex 12:10)
R' Akiva needs הזה because from that verse alone one would say 'morning' means the second morning
R' Elazar could say: every [unqualified] 'morning' is the first morning
the dispute of these tannaim (R' Elazar ben Azarya / R' Akiva) is the dispute of those tannaim (R' Eliezer / R' Yehoshua on Deut 16:6)
'in the evening' (Deut 16:6) -- you slaughter
'when the sun sets' -- you eat
R' Eliezer: 'at the time you left Egypt' -- you burn [what remains]
R' Yehoshua: and until when do you go on eating? until 'the time you left Egypt'
all agree: when Israel were redeemed from Egypt they were redeemed only in the evening -- 'the Lord your God brought you out of Egypt at night' (Deut 16:1)
and when they left, they left only by day -- 'on the day after the Pesach the children of Israel went out with a high hand' (Num 33:3)
what they disagree about is the hour of haste
R' Elazar ben Azarya holds: 'haste' is the haste of the Egyptians
R' Akiva holds: 'haste' is the haste of Israel
the baraita: 'brought you out of Egypt at night' -- did they leave at night? they left by day (Num 33:3)! rather, it teaches that the redemption began for them in the evening
